topic: How should the skill advisor surface slash commands (all 45 under .skilled/commands, not only /doctor) so a model either runs the matching command workflow by itself or asks the user first, and how does a request typed as plain chat with no slash command still reach the proper command workflow on every runtime? Work through ten research angles: inventory, scoring, output contract, run or ask, invocation mechanics, chat-only users, skill and command linkage, measurement, prior art, and failure modes.

normalized_topic: how should the skill advisor surface slash commands all 45 under skilled commands not only doctor so a model either runs the matching command workflow by itself or asks the user first and how does a request typed as plain chat with no slash command still reach the proper command workflow on every runtime

focus: Angle 1: Inventory, reconcile the 45 command files with bridge sources and runtime-enabled bridge identities.
Angle 2: Scoring. Examine how command and skill intent combine, how plain-chat and typed-command evidence affect rank, and how eligibility and run-or-ask gates interact.
Angle 3: Output contract. Inspect the current advisor brief and command-rendering surfaces, then specify what a model needs to load or ask across all commands.
Angle 4: Run or ask. Separate workflow selection from required command inputs, execution modes, spec routing choices and high-impact approvals.
Angle 5: Invocation mechanics. Trace how plain prompts reach the advisor and how the resulting command or skill workflow can be loaded across supported runtimes.
Angle 6: Plain-chat-only users. Determine how ordinary language reaches command routes and where the current fallback or runtime coverage leaves gaps.
Angle 7: Skill and command linkage. Compare source-level user intent/choreography with bridge identity, owner mode and model-visible routing.
Angle 8: Measurement. Assess available route corpora, scoring metrics, ambiguous cases, command coverage and runtime evidence.
Angle 9: Prior art. Compare explicit slash command catalogs, metadata-driven plain-language skill activation, evaluation practice and host-specific invocation constraints.
Angle 10: Failure modes. Inspect over/under-triggering, command-skill ambiguity, child recursion, loop stops and prompt-budget loss.
